record.context_brief: Associativity of the asymptotic Hecke algebra
record.original_question: Assume the boundedness hypothesis that there is an integer N >= 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} is in Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z in W, where the basis elements c_w satisfy c_x c_y = sum_{z in W} h_{x,y,z} c_z. For each z in W, let a(z) be the unique integer >= 0 such that every h_{x,y,z} lies in v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] and, for at least one pair x, y, the same coefficient h_{x,y,z} does not lie in v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Define integers gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} by h_{x,y,z} = gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)} modulo v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]. Let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w : w in W}, and define multiplication on basis elements by t_x t_y = sum_{z in W} gamma_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z. Does this multiplication make J into an associative ring, not necessarily with an identity element?

evidence.quote: For x, y in W we set txty = P z∈W γx,y,z−1 tz.
(c) Show that this defines an (associative) ring structure on J (without 1 in general).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (W,S) be a Coxeter system with weight function L, and let H be the associated Iwahori–Hecke algebra over Z[v,v^{-1}] with Kazhdan–Lusztig basis {c_w : w ∈ W}. Write the structure constants

  c_x c_y = Σ_{z ∈ W} h_{x,y,z} c_z,   h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v,v^{-1}].

Assume the boundedness hypothesis: there exists an integer N ≥ 0 such that v^{-N} h_{x,y,z} ∈ Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y, z ∈ W.

For each z ∈ W, define a(z) to be the unique nonnegative integer such that
 (i) h_{x,y,z} ∈ v^{a(z)} Z[v^{-1}] for all x, y ∈ W, and
 (ii) there exist x, y ∈ W with h_{x,y,z} ∉ v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}].

Define integers γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} ∈ Z by the congruence
  h_{x,y,z} ≡ γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} v^{a(z)}  (mod v^{a(z)-1} Z[v^{-1}]).

Let J be the free abelian group with basis {t_w : w ∈ W}, and define a Z-bilinear product on J by
  t_x t_y = Σ_{z ∈ W} γ_{x,y,z^{-1}} t_z.

Question: Does this product endow J with the structure of an associative ring (not required to have a multiplicative identity)?
artifact.status_search_result: Associativity of J is known to follow from Lusztig's conjectures P1–P15, and these conjectures are established in significant cases (e.g., equal-parameter finite and affine Weyl groups, and certain other settings) where boundedness is known. However, for general Coxeter groups with arbitrary positive weight function, P1–P15 — and hence the associativity of J in full generality — remain open. Recent work (e.g., on boundedness of the a-function for Coxeter groups of finite rank) extends the cases where the construction is valid, but the question is not settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of Lusztig's a-function for Coxeter groups of finite rank
status_evidence.snippet: In cases where boundedness is established, Lusztig's conjectures P1–P15 are proved; J is associative under these assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Associativity of J is tied to P1–P15, which depend on boundedness; not yet established for all Coxeter groups with arbitrary weights.

status_evidence.title: Remarks on the asymptotic Hecke algebra
status_evidence.snippet: Lusztig defined an associative algebra J implementing the independence on q of the representation theory of H.
status_evidence.claim: J is known to be associative in cases where Lusztig's P1–P15 conjectures hold.
